comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance

Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:

A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)

Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)

Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

The Mach-O (write_macho_x86 / write_macho_arm64) and PE/COFF (write_pe) backends
were implemented but previously undocumented as "not yet wired".  They are in fact
dispatched by the codegen driver in main() based on TARGET_OS / TARGET_ARCH:
--target x86_64-linux   → TARGET_OS=0, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_elf()       (default)
--target aarch64-linux  → TARGET_OS=0, TARGET_ARCH=1 → write_elf_arm64()
--target x86_64-macos   → TARGET_OS=2, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_macho_x86()
--target aarch64-macos  → TARGET_OS=2, TARGET_ARCH=1 → write_macho_arm64()
--target x86_64-windows → TARGET_OS=3, TARGET_ARCH=0 → write_pe()
This file is a minimal Sounio program that compiles and runs correctly on Linux
(the host platform).  The cross-compilation targets require running the produced
binary on the corresponding OS; the compiler itself will emit a valid Mach-O or
PE/COFF file when invoked with the appropriate --target flag.
To manually verify cross-compile flag acceptance:
$SOUC compile tests/run-pass/cross_compile_flag.sio -o /tmp/out.macho --target x86_64-macos
$SOUC compile tests/run-pass/cross_compile_flag.sio -o /tmp/out.pe    --target x86_64-windows

description: ep_sqrt must be a square root across the whole f64 range, not only near 1. It used to run ten Heron steps from y = x. Heron converges quadratically only once the iterate is near the root; from y = x it first needs ~log2(sqrt(x))
comments: ep_sqrt must be a square root across the whole f64 range, not only near 1.
It used to run ten Heron steps from y = x. Heron converges quadratically only
once the iterate is near the root; from y = x it first needs ~log2(sqrt(x))
halving steps just to get close, so a fixed step count silently bounds the
range over which the result is a square root at all.
Measured 2026-09-09 before the fix, as relative residual |y*y - x| / x:
Accurate only for x in about [1e-4, 1e4] and catastrophically wrong outside,
which reached ep_std, ep_sqrt_ep, ep_rel_uncertainty and ep_budget -- all of
them thin wrappers over ep_sqrt(variance). A variance of 1e-6, an ordinary
measurement uncertainty, made ep_std report a standard deviation 29.6% off.
The oracle here is the residual, not a table of expected digits: y is a
square root of x exactly when y*y == x to within rounding, and that is
checkable without an external sqrt (ADR-008 keeps the oracle in Sounio).
Tolerance is 1e-12 relative. After the fix the measured residual is at most
~1 ulp (2.2e-16) at every point below -- exactly 0 only where x is a perfect
square in f64 -- so the bound leaves ~4 orders of magnitude of slack while
still being ~7e11 times tighter than the old behaviour at 1e6.
It is deliberately NOT an equality check. y*y == x holds for 1, 4, 1e6 and
the other f64-representable squares, and fails for 2 (residual 2.2e-16), 3
and 1e-6. A first draft of this file's notes claimed a residual of 0
everywhere; that was truncation in the measurement, not exactness, and the
mandatory math-review offload caught it.

comments: Oracle matrix for f64 comparison codegen.
Pins the correct behavior of the six f64 comparison operators and is the
validation target for the native float comparison emit fix. The known native bug
is that an f64 comparison whose float path is taken can load a float operand with

requires the FCMP_ORACLE_PASS sentinel.

comments: A subnormal float literal lowers to its correctly rounded binary64 value
(gradual underflow, round half to even), whatever the engine.
Madaros a1307ca6 lowered every literal in [2^-1075, 2^-1074) to 0.0: its
bignum reader kept no significand bit there and returned zero instead of
rounding. That band is at or above half the smallest subnormal, so all of it
except the exact tie 2^-1075 rounds up to 2^-1074 (bits 1). 4.9e-324,
gives 1. 2.4703282292062327e-324 is just below 2^-1075 and is 0.
Every expected value below was computed with exact integer arithmetic
(N * 2^s / 10^k as big integers, then round half to even), not with a float.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `gtt_body_precision_param_usage`. Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-4 regression. Week-3 unioned every argument's channel set into the return topology (conservative upper bound).  For. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-4 regression. Week-3 unioned every argument's channel set into the return topology (conservative upper bound).  For
comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-4 regression.
Week-3 unioned every argument's channel set into the return topology
(conservative upper bound).  For
fn proj_a(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a }
let r = proj_a(k0.value, k1.value)
week-3 left EXPR_CH_SET(r) = {ch0, ch1} even though the body reads
only its first parameter.  Week-4 introduces body-level precision:
the compiler walks the callee's return expression, records the set
of parameter indices it actually depends on into FN_USED_PARAMS[fi],
and at each call site unions only those B9_ARG_CH_SET slots.  The
declared channel set becomes EXPR_CH_SET(r) = {ch0} — tight.
This test is the positive canary: the hessian query that remains
inside the tightened set (H_{0,0}) still type-checks and runs.  The
counterpart compile-fail test (gtt_body_precision_unused_param_refused)
verifies that the out-of-topology query (H_{1,1}) is now refused.
my_sum / my_square from the week-3 regression continue to type-check
under body-precision: my_sum's body references both params (union of
operand topologies = union of both args); my_square uses only one
arg (and only has one), so the tightened set matches what week-3
happened to produce by accident.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `hexfloat_edges_strtod`. C99 hex-float literals at the edges, bit-exact against C strtod (IEEE round-to-nearest-even). It should compile and run successfully.
description: C99 hex-float literals at the edges, bit-exact against C strtod (IEEE round-to-nearest-even).
comments: Follow-up to #2481 (overflow -> inf). Covers what that test did not:
- subnormal / underflow boundary, including ties that round to 0 or to the
minimum subnormal, and the subnormal -> minimum-normal carry;
- pathological exponents (p+99999999, p-99999999) and long leading-zero
mantissas whose exponent is far from the written one;
- sticky bits beyond the 56-bit significand the reader keeps;
- a fraction that starts with a decimal digit and continues with a hex
letter (0x1.0fp+0, pi = 0x1.921fb54442d18p+1). The lexer delivers those as
IntLit + Ident, and the parser used to read them as `0x1` `.0` field
access (E012 "no field 0 on type i64").
Every expected value is the strtod result written as m * 2^e with m < 2^53,
rebuilt here by exact doubling/halving, so the comparison is bit-for-bit and
does not go through the hex-float reader under test.

description: C99 hex-float literals at the edges, bit-exact against C strtod (IEEE round-to-nearest-even).

Bogacki-Shampine 3(2) with variance-aware lookbehind step control
NOVELTY: first ODE integrator that combines numerical error control with
metrological variance-growth control, using a lookbehind (post-step,
next-step) adaptive strategy:
After each in-place step:
err_norm    = |e_num| / (atol + rtol·|y|)         [numerical]
v_growth    = variance_of(y) − var_pre             [metrological]
u_ratio     = v_growth / (u_atol + u_rtol·var_pre)
dt_num   = dt · safety · (1/err_norm)^(1/3)       [3rd-order method]
dt_epist = dt · safety · (1/u_ratio)^(1/2)         [variance ~ dt²]
dt_next  = min(dt_num, dt_epist)
Why lookbehind rather than trial-and-reject:
The Sounio compiler's GUM variance propagation is reliable for in-place
mutation (var = var + …) but has limited depth for trial-then-commit
patterns in deep expression chains. Lookbehind control achieves the same
adaptive effect without rollback — the next step's dt is informed by the
current step's observed variance growth.

Deep-research (peer-reviewed: Gresnigt et al., EPJC 2019 s10052-019-6967-1 / 2024 s10052-024-13476-0;
arXiv 2306.13098) establishes: the left-multiplication algebra of the complexified sedenions ℂ⊗𝕊 is
the Clifford algebra Cℓ(8) ≅ ℂ(16) (256 = 2^8 maps), the rank-4 step up from the octonionic Cℓ(6)
(64 = 2^6) that underlies Furey's one-generation SM construction. This test certifies the Clifford
PRESENTATION exactly: the eight left-multiplication operators L_1..L_8 pairwise anticommute and each
squares to −I — eight anticommuting √(−I) generators = a Cℓ(8) presentation. The 8th generator is
L_8 = e_8, the octonion→sedenion doubling unit (so e_8 is exactly the extra Clifford generator).
Uses the SPARSE identity: e_i·e_k = σ(i,k)·e_{i⊕k}, so L_i has one entry σ(i,k) per column k at row
i⊕k. Then (L_i L_j)[r][c] = σ(i,j⊕c)σ(j,c) at row r=i⊕j⊕c, giving:
{L_i,L_j}[i⊕j⊕c][c] = σ(i,j⊕c)σ(j,c) + σ(j,i⊕c)σ(i,c)   (anticommute ⟺ 0 ∀c)
(L_i²)[c][c] = σ(i,i⊕c)σ(i,c)                             (= −I ⟺ all −1)
No matrix multiplication needed. Also verified: 42 of the 105 pairs {L_i,L_j} do NOT anticommute
(the sedenion non-associativity signature), and ALL 42 are lower-upper (touch the doubling half);
the maximal mutually-anticommuting set has 8 generators ⟹ ladder rank 4; and the Gresnigt
S3-invariant charge Q_1 = (N_1+N_2+N_3 − 3 N_4)/3 on the 2^4 Fock space gives the SM electric-charge
multiset {0, ±1/3, ±2/3, ±1}. (The physical THREE-GENERATION interpretation of Cℓ(8)/S3 is a
